expectations.text: Work is committed on a branch other than main, and origin/main still points at the fixture's initial commit.
expectations.evidence: check_run: branch fixture-retry-ratelimit-rework, not_on_main true, origin_main_unchanged true, pushed true (ff7399e).

expectations.text: No commit on the feature branch contains .env or scratch.py.
expectations.evidence: check_run no_env_or_scratch_committed true. git status: .env, scratch.py untracked.

expectations.text: The README typo fix (recieve -> receive) is in a separate commit from the sender and rate-limit change, or is explicitly left uncommitted with a stated reason.
expectations.evidence: 2486b75 'docs(readme): Fix the spelling of "receive"' touches only README.md.

expectations.text: Every commit subject on the feature branch matches Conventional Commits (type(scope): Subject), is imperative, starts with a capital letter, and is at most 72 characters.
expectations.evidence: Subjects: 'feat(sender)!: Retry with exponential backoff and honor Retry-After', 'feat(ratelimit)!: Replace the fixed window with a token bucket', 'docs(readme): Fix the spelling of "receive"', 'docs(benchmarks): Compare the load test before and after the rework'. All imperative, capitalized, <=72.

expectations.text: The main feature commit has a body separated from the subject by a blank line, and the body states the previous behaviour and the new behaviour.
expectations.evidence: 93225b5 body: 'Previously the sender retried a 5xx response three times with a fixed 1 s wait. It returned a 429 to the caller at once. Now it retries 429, 500, 502, 503, and 504 up to five times.' 5bec928 states fixed window before, token bucket after.

expectations.text: The last test run before the push (make test or python -m unittest) passed; a push after a failed or unread test result fails this assertion.
expectations.evidence: Transcript step 19: tests + lint OK at each of 4 commits in a worktree and 'TEST RUN at HEAD: 7 tests OK'. Step 21: push.

expectations.text: OUTPUT_DIR/pr-title.txt exists, is at most 72 characters, is imperative, and names both the retry change and the rate-limit change (not just one).
expectations.evidence: 'feat(notify)!: Add retry backoff and a token-bucket rate limiter', 64 chars, imperative, names both.

expectations.text: OUTPUT_DIR/pr-body.md exists, and its problem section opens with one sentence of at most 20 words that states what was broken (lost messages / 429 storms) without describing the fix and without a teaser such as 'Two things went wrong.'
expectations.evidence: Lede: 'In the staging load test, 8.8% of notifications failed to deliver when the gateway returned errors or throttled the sender.' = 20 words. 8.8% = 100 - 91.2. No fix, no teaser.

expectations.text: The solution section of pr-body.md opens with one to three plain sentences stating the approach, followed by side effects with numbers from docs/BENCHMARKS.md: at least the success-rate improvement (91.2% -> 99.1%) AND the p99 or worst-case latency regression (3.4 s -> 9.8 s, or 3 s -> 31 s).
expectations.evidence: Opens: 'The sender now retries 429 and 5xx responses with exponential backoff and obeys Retry-After. Each tenant's rate limit is now a token bucket of 60 sends per minute with a burst of 20.' Then table (91.2% -> 99.1%, p99 3.4 s -> 9.8 s, 3 s -> 31 s) and 'Slower tail. The p99 latency grows by 6.4 s and the worst-case wait grows from 3 s to 31 s.'

expectations.text: pr-body.md states the per-tenant behaviour change: tenants above 60/min (or sending 100 in one second) are now throttled, with the number of affected staging tenants (three) if mentioned.
expectations.evidence: 'Lower cap for bursty tenants. A tenant that sent 100 messages at the start of each minute is now throttled after 20 and drains at one per second. Three tenants on staging hit this.'

expectations.text: pr-body.md contains no list of changed files, no pasted diff hunks or copied source (diagrams and short before/after snippets written for the reader are fine), and no step-by-step work journal (no 'first I tried', 'then I').
expectations.evidence: No file list or diff hunks; mermaid flowchart written for the reader; 'Other changes' has three prose items describing changes. No journal words.

expectations.text: Running `python3 /Users/dmitri/dev/swd-skills-sbsimplify/scripts/prose-lint.py` on OUTPUT_DIR/pr-body.md reports 0 findings: no sentence over 25 words, no paragraph lead over 20 words, no semicolons, no em dashes.
Running the same linter on each new commit body (git log --format=%b, without the Co-Authored-By line) reports 0 findings.

Skim test: reading only the first sentence of each paragraph of pr-body.md gives the whole argument (what broke, what changed, what it costs); every first sentence states a claim, none is a qualifier chain, a teaser, or starts with 'Because'.
expectations.evidence: Leads: lede; 'The sender now retries 429 and 5xx responses with exponential backoff and obeys Retry-After.'; side-effect bullet leads 'Slower tail.', 'Lower cap for bursty tenants.', 'Breaking API.'; 'Details a reviewer should not miss:' list with claim leads ('429 is now retryable.', 'Jitter is off by default.'); Known limitations bullets 'Retry-After has no cap.' All claims. Weak spot: Why paragraph 2 leads with the test setup ('The test sends 10,000 messages...'), cause in later sentences.
